definition: Design Automation usually refers to electronic design automation, or Design Automation which is a Product Configurator.
details: Extending Computer-Aided Design (CAD), automated design and Computer-Automated Design (CAutoD) are more concerned with a broader range of applications, such as automotive engineering, civil engineering, composite material design, control engineering, dynamic system identification and optimization, financial systems, industrial equipment, mechatronic systems, steel construction, structural optimisation, and the invention of novel systems. The concept of CAutoD perhaps first appeared in 1963, in the IBM Journal of Research and Development, where a computer program was written. to search for logic circuits having certain constraints on hardware design to evaluate these logics in terms of their discriminating ability over samples of the character set they are expected to recognize. More recently, traditional CAD simulation is seen to be transformed to CAutoD by biologically-inspired machine learning, including heuristic search techniques such as evolutionary computation, and swarm intelligence algorithms.

explainer.lead: Computer-automated design (CAutoD) extends computer-aided design by letting a computer generate, test, and improve candidate designs rather than only helping people draw or simulate them. It matters because the same search-based approach can tackle problems ranging from structural optimisation to control engineering and the invention of novel systems.

tiers.eli5: Imagine asking a computer to build the best paper bridge instead of merely drawing one for you. It could try different shapes, check which ones hold the most weight without breaking your rules, and then use what it learns to try better shapes. That is the basic idea of computer-automated design.
tiers.practitioner: CAutoD combines design modelling and simulation with biologically inspired machine learning, notably evolutionary computation and swarm intelligence. Engineers define the design choices, constraints, and performance criteria, then let heuristic search generate and evaluate successive candidates. Applications include automotive and civil engineering, composite materials, mechatronics, steel construction, and dynamic system identification and optimisation.
tiers.paperLevel: CAutoD can be expressed as searching for x* = arg min f(x) subject to design constraints C(x), where x represents a candidate design and f(x) is evaluated through criteria such as simulation. CAD modelling and simulation are augmented by heuristic search methods, including evolutionary computation and swarm intelligence. The concept may first have appeared in the IBM Journal of Research and Development in 1963, in a program that searched hardware-constrained logic circuits and evaluated their ability to discriminate among character samples.

explainer.example: In the 1963 logic-circuit example, a computer program searched for circuits that satisfied hardware-design constraints. It evaluated candidate logic by how well it discriminated among samples of the character set the circuits were expected to recognise.

usedIn.name: Automotive engineering
usedIn.detail: Applies automated design search and evaluation beyond conventional CAD simulation.

usedIn.detail: Searches candidate structures against specified design goals and constraints.

usedIn.name: Composite material design
usedIn.detail: Explores and evaluates alternative material designs computationally.

usedIn.name: Control engineering

explainer.intuition: CAD helps a person represent and simulate a design; CAutoD adds a search process that proposes alternatives and uses their evaluations to look for better ones. The computer therefore takes part in design exploration, not just documentation and analysis.
howItWorks: Specify the design variables, goals, hardware or engineering constraints, and evaluation criteria.
Generate candidate designs across the permitted search space.
Simulate or otherwise evaluate each candidate against the stated criteria.
Use heuristic search, such as evolutionary computation or swarm intelligence, to propose improved candidates.
Repeat the generate-and-evaluate cycle and select a design that performs well under the constraints.
explainer.whyItMatters: Automating design search allows computers to explore candidates across many engineering domains instead of relying solely on manually proposed alternatives. It also connects CAD simulation with optimisation methods that can support structural improvement and the invention of novel systems.
misconceptions: CAutoD is not simply another name for CAD: it adds automated generation, search, and improvement to modelling and simulation.
It is not limited to electronic design automation; its applications span automotive, civil, materials, control, industrial, and mechatronic engineering.
Design Automation can also refer to a product configurator, which is a different use of the term.
